svg.title: Step 13 · Evals and release
svg.desc: Thirteen golden questions are asked of the live site as the page asks them, one at a time; each answer is graded by rules on the tools it called and the words it says or never says; with LangSmith's key, the questions become a dataset and each run an experiment named for the build. A small load test times the page, the health check and a few questions. Rolling back uses Vercel's Instant Rollback, then a revert in git. The Technical details page follows one question through the code, and the backup tag is deleted, its commit kept in the history.
svg.text: Step 13 · Evals and release
Grade what the answers do, time what the site does, and know how to go back
13 golden questions
a place, now, forecast, air
several matches, none, too far
units, off-topic, the rules
a storm: never "you're safe"
Asked of the live site, graded
as the page asks, one at a time, 8 s apart
the tools its chips name, in order
words it must say, or never say
a rule, not a model: the same every run
LangSmith, with its key
the dataset nimbus-golden
each run an experiment,
named for the build
nothing asked twice
A small load test: 40 pages, 40 health checks, 3 questions, 8 at once
each timed to its last byte; for each kind, how many, how many failed, p50, p95, slowest
cold starts show in the slowest; Gemini's quota, not Vercel, is where a free app stops
Rolling back
Vercel: Instant Rollback, in seconds,
nothing rebuilt; new pushes wait
git: revert, push; CI and the deploy run
a tag a step: py-step-01 to py-step-13
And the rebuild, finished
Technical details: one question through the code,
with the seven lines it left in Axiom
the backup tag deleted: its commit, c7165ac,
stays in main's history
In the tests: the app's own stream read, in this process; each rule; LangSmith played back;
a small load against the app in this process, a question that fails counted as failed
Grade what an answer does, not how it's worded; practise going back before you need to.
Keeping the evals in LangSmith, and a rollback once: Waiting on you.
